title: Ethiopian Spiced Corn on the Cob
community: Ethiopian markets and streets — the roasted corn vendor
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Roasted Corn — fresh corn on the cob roasted directly over charcoal until the kernels char lightly, rubbed with lemon, salt, and mitmita. The universal African street food given its Ethiopian character by the mitmita rub.
longDesc: Roasted corn is the most universal street food in sub-Saharan Africa, and Ethiopian roasted corn gets its distinctive character from the mitmita and lemon rub — the fierce heat of mitmita and the acidity of lemon transform it from ordinary to extraordinary.
steps: Soak corn cobs in water 10 minutes.
Place directly over charcoal, husks on.
Remove husks when cool enough to handle.
Mix mitmita and salt. Squeeze lemon over corn.
chefTips: The husks char on the outside while steaming the corn inside — perfect cooking.
Apply mitmita and lemon while hot.
commonMistakes: Not soaking — husks burn before corn cooks.
cookingScience: See TZA256 for corn roasting science. The Ethiopian mitmita rub combines capsaicin (which activates heat receptors) with the citric acid from lemon (which activates acid-sensing receptors) simultaneously — the combined sensory stimulation is more intense than either alone.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian highland corn — grown without irrigation in the rainy season.
culturalNote: Ethiopian roasted corn with mitmita is the harvest season street food that brings together the two elements that define Ethiopian street food — fire and fierce spice. The vendor's charcoal with corn cobs turning on it is the visual signature of Ethiopian market season.
